purpose: Durable, machine-readable classification of every database object that `tsc --noEmit` rejects on d2176904, so each owning domain can fix its own share without re-deriving the analysis. This is the deliverable the release, qa and venue lanes asked for; it supersedes the ad-hoc per-lane object lists in HF-QA-003-TYPECHECK-BLOCKER, HF-RELEASE-DB-TYPECHECK and HF-DB-008-VENUE-CREW-CONTRACTOR-SURFACE.

howToRead.stale-types: The active chain creates the object and lib/database.types.ts does not declare it. Fix = regenerate the types from a reconciled target. Never fixable by hand-editing the generated file.
howToRead.schema-missing: Neither the active chain nor the generated types have the object, and the repository holds no archived definition, so the product code is right and the chain needs a new additive forward-only migration. Only objects whose contract is unambiguous from the repository were migrated in this wave; the rest need the owning domain's column contract first.
howToRead.code-drift: The object exists only in archived or out-of-chain SQL, or the repository names a different canonical replacement, so the active chain deliberately never created it. Fix = repoint or remove the consumer. conflictLiveConsumer = true means a LIVE entry-reachable route or page depends on it, so deleting the module is not an option and an owner decision is required before anything is removed.
howToRead.unknown: Genuinely undecidable from the repository: absent everywhere, no canonical replacement recorded, and every consumer unreachable. Recorded rather than guessed.

evidenceMethod.diagnosticsSource: The preserved GitHub Actions log of the failing `Lint And Build` job on d2176904: 1,384 primary diagnostics across 407 files (TS2339 x495, TS2769 x265, TS2322 x180, TS2589 x163, TS2345 x161, TS18047 x26, remainder x195). Objects are read out of the exact tsc message: `Argument of type '"<name>"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"..." | ...'` for .from()/.rpc() overload resolution, and `column '<c>' does not exist on '<t>'` for column drift.
evidenceMethod.chainSurfaceMethod: An ordered CREATE/DROP/RENAME event replay over the numbered files in supabase/migrations/, comment-, string-literal- and dollar-quote-aware, so the answer is the schema the chain would actually leave behind rather than a bag of greps. Objects created only inside a DO/$$...$$ body are recorded separately as dynamic-only and are never claimed as chain-created.
evidenceMethod.nonActiveEvidenceMethod: Every .sql file in the repository that is not an active numbered migration: supabase/migrations/archive/, supabase/migrations_backup/, supabase/migration-archive/, the legacy root-level scripts and scripts/.
evidenceMethod.consumerLivenessMethod: A consumer file is LIVE when it is a Next.js entry point (route/page/layout/loading/error/not-found/template/default, middleware, instrumentation) or is imported by one. Otherwise it is DEAD, meaning nothing reachable can execute it.
evidenceMethod.notClaimed: No tsc run was performed by this lane: a full `npm run typecheck` is prohibited in a four-lane wave and OOMs on this machine. The counts are read out of the preserved CI log and the chain/types verdicts are static. No migration was applied and no hosted evidence is claimed.

knownGaps.detail: The log contains 173 lines carrying SelectQueryError. 144 of them include the full `column '<c>' does not exist on '<t>'` text and are classified here. The remaining 29 are truncated inside the printed union, so the table cannot be recovered from the log alone. They are the same defect class and need a scoped tsc run to enumerate.
knownGaps.resolution: owner-scoped typecheck after the code-drift clusters are fixed

knownGaps.gap: Type-level diagnostics that name no object
knownGaps.detail: TS2589 (163), TS2322 (180), TS7006/TS2739/TS2353/TS2352 and the residual tail name no Supabase object. They are very largely downstream of the same defect: a relation missing from the generated contract makes PostgREST's builder resolve to an error type, which produces the deep-instantiation and assignability noise. Their exact reduction can only be measured by a real tsc run, which this lane did not perform.
knownGaps.resolution: re-run npm run typecheck after the clusters are fixed and compare against this baseline

knownGaps.gap: RETRACTED — the generated contract IS reproducible from the active chain
knownGaps.detail: Wave 33 reported 130 contract columns across 23 relations with no chain provenance, headlined by public.venue_profiles (42 declared, 19 created). That was an instrument defect, not schema drift. The Wave 33 column replay matched `add column` case-SENSITIVELY inside matchAll(), so every migration written in upper-case DDL style contributed zero columns, it recorded the keyword `constraint` as a column name, it did not model `alter table if exists` no-ops, and it applied DROP and CREATE events in per-kind loop order rather than file order. A corrected replay (supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs) reconstructs 401 tables + 14 views, 5335 columns and 224 routines from the 305-migration chain and finds ZERO contract columns, ZERO contract relations and ZERO contract callables without chain provenance. public.venue_profiles resolves to 44 chain columns, every one attributed to a named active migration; 5170 contract columns were independently re-verified against the cited file (supabase/tests/db008_contract_attribution_audit.mjs, 0 unsupported).
knownGaps.resolution: CLOSED for the deletion risk. CP-016 regeneration can no longer remove contract coverage: the chain is a strict superset. Regeneration is still blocked on OPERATIONAL grounds only (no linked or project-id target, Docker unavailable, so `supabase gen types` cannot run here) and on the marketplace relations, which until 20260926120000/120100 are absent from BOTH the chain and the contract and therefore cannot appear in any regeneration.

knownGaps.gap: View column surface is proven by name occurrence, not by replay
knownGaps.detail: 13 of the 415 chain relations are views or materialized views. A view column list is the SELECT list of its definition, which no text replay reconstructs reliably (joins, aliases, select *). For those 13 the contract surface is checked by literal column-name occurrence in the migration that defines the view; all 13 views currently have 0 columns without a name occurrence. That is weaker than the table-column replay and is the one place where a regeneration could still remove coverage.
knownGaps.resolution: If a future regeneration drops a view column, check this surface first. Reconstructing the 13 definitions by replay is possible but was judged lower value than the marketplace and contract work in this wave.

knownGaps.gap: Six ALTERs are skipped by a fresh chain replay
knownGaps.detail: Version order is not calendar order, so 20250904110000 (2025-09-04) runs BEFORE 20260413200000 (2026-04-13). 20250813121000 ALTERs public.staff_invitations four times and 20250904110000 / 20250905004500 ALTER public.scheduled_posts, all inside to_regclass or information_schema guards, at points where those relations do not yet exist. A fresh replay therefore skips all six; the staff_invitations columns still arrive from the later CREATE, and the two scheduled_posts columns (platform_status, platform_errors) are absent from both the chain and the contract, so the two agree. A LIVE target that received the tables earlier may carry platform_status / platform_errors, which a chain-built target will not — a live-versus-fresh divergence that regeneration would remove.
knownGaps.resolution: Operator decision before the next regeneration: does any live target carry scheduled_posts.platform_status? If yes, capture it as an additive migration (or confirm it is dead) rather than letting regeneration delete it. Recorded as a handoff.

diagnosticHitCountMethod: tscDiagnosticHits counts, per object, the number of primary diagnostics whose 8-line message window names that object. Because tsc repeats the rejected literal inside the printed overload union, those per-object hits SUM TO MORE than the 1,384 primary diagnostics (1,548 here) and must never be added up and read as a diagnostic total. The authoritative totals are 1,384 primary diagnostics across 407 files and 128 distinct missing objects. 197 distinct file paths appear on the primary diagnostic lines; the 407 figure is tsc's own end-of-run summary, which also counts files that only produced suppressed or warning-level output.

staleTypeSurface.note: Objects the active chain creates and lib/database.types.ts does not declare. The chain is now 305 migrations: 415 relations (401 tables + 14 views), 224 routines (142 callable + 82 trigger). RETURNS trigger functions are correctly never emitted by `supabase gen types`, so they are counted separately and are not drift. Regeneration would ADD every item below and remove nothing.
staleTypeSurface.stalenessWatermark: The contract reflects the chain through 20260910000001_get_active_organizer_account_for_org.sql. Everything listed here is created by a later migration and would be added by regeneration. Note that cleanup_orphaned_artist_files, cleanup_old_notifications and refresh_forum_mviews are created in 2025 and are STILL absent from the contract: they remain an unexplained generation-target artefact, now 39 callables rather than 4, so the Wave 33 reading that they were mostly staleness does not hold.
staleTypeSurface.wave34Correction: Wave 33 listed 4 unexplained callables (cleanup_orphaned_artist_files, cleanup_old_notifications, refresh_forum_mviews, fix_missing_profiles) alongside 15 stale ones. With the corrected 100-callable contract count, fix_missing_profiles IS present in the contract and 39 callables are chain-only, of which those three 2025 functions remain the genuinely unexplained minority.
